header: Date: 2026-03-03 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 47m | Location: Zoom | Recording: available\nRedwood: Jordan Lee (AE), Priya Raman (SE) | Aegis Pharma: Dr. Maria Sanchez (CTO), Evan Cole (Head Infra), Ravi Patel (Security), Nia Brooks (QA)
summary: Discovery focused on requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped private deployment. Main concerns: offline/air-gapped update process, hardware compatibility (GPU types, NVLink), KMS/HSM integration, auditability, and validation windows. Redwood AE/SE walked through architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), fallback strategies, and typical security controls for regulated pharma workloads. Customer wants proof run with their hardware and detailed offline upgrade playbook before procurement.
topics: hardware constraints (A100 vs H100, NVLink / PCIe)
network isolation and on-prem control plane
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. We're Jordan from Redwood Inference - with me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Good morning. Thanks for the invite. We have a few people from infra and security on the call to go over air-gapped options.
[00:25] Evan Cole: Hey, Evan here. Quick context: we're evaluating options for running LLM inference in our on-prem data center, completely isolated. No egress allowed except via change window.
[00:40] Priya Raman: Got it. We'll walk through our Private deployment story and then do a deeper dive on the offline update pipeline and hardware compatibility.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: Two top constraints for us: 1) updates must be applied via an internal media or signed artifact with attestable provenance, and 2) we need KMS/HSM integration for model keys.

[01:30] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. That aligns with what we've done for other regulated customers - we provide signed bundles and an offline install tool. We can integrate with customer HSMs for key wrapping.
[01:55] Nia Brooks: Also, from QA: we need a deterministic rollout and a way to run model regression tests in an offline lab before going to production. How do you handle that?

[02:10] Priya Raman: We recommend a canary in a segregated VLAN - in air-gapped setups that's often a physically separate rack or lab. We provide a manifest you can run that verifies model outputs against your baseline prompts. There's a test harness we can ship as part of the bundle.
[02:35] Dr. Maria Sanchez: When you say "bundle" - is that a container image, or a set of binaries? What's updated during a patch?

[02:50] Jordan Lee: Good question. It's typically a tarball with versioned artifacts: runtime binaries, model weights (optionally in quantized form), a signed manifest, and a script for staged install. Customers can also bring their own image. For strict air-gapped installs we support an offline verification step using public key signatures.
[03:15] Evan Cole: We have both A100s and some H100s in our fleet, but NVLink is only available on the H100 nodes. Any constraints around that?

[03:30] Priya Raman: Runtime will auto-select kernels based on the hardware. For multi-GPU with NVLink we route large context jobs there; otherwise single GPU paths use optimized kernels. We also document any kernel dependencies - sometimes CUDA minor versions matter.
[04:00] Ravi Patel: How do you handle telemetry? We can't have outbound telemetry to Redwood. We need logs to be stored locally and we may ship them on tape during audits. Is that supported?

[04:15] Jordan Lee: Yes - Private deployments can operate with zero outbound telemetry. We provide an offline log export tool and local tracing. Optionally, a signed bundle can enable an asynchronous pull-by-push model if you want to push audit packages to a jump box during maintenance windows.
[04:40] Nia Brooks: Any guidance on acceptance testing? We want to run a regression suite of prompts and measure latency and token-level differences.

[04:55] Priya Raman: We can provide a benchmark harness with representative prompt sets. For pharma customers we often include deterministic evaluation and BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics for structured output. We'll also suggest a token sampling seed for consistency. Note: sampling-based models can have nondeterminism unless you use a deterministic decoder or seed fixed RNG.
[05:25] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Security: SSO / SAML integration for admin console and RBAC for operators - do you expose a control plane we must lock down?

[05:40] Jordan Lee: The Private deployment ships with a customer-managed control plane. You host the control plane in your VPC/on-prem environment. We support SAML and OIDC for admin auth, and you can restrict APIs to internal subnets. We also support per-token auditing for requests.
[06:05] Evan Cole: For model updates, how is the model signed and verified? Where do keys live?

[06:20] Priya Raman: Models are signed by Redwood with a release key, and you validate signatures with a public key; for higher assurance customers we support HSM-backed signing on your side or integrate with your HSM for key wrapping. The recommended pattern is we provide the signed artifact and you verify in-place using your root of trust.
[06:50] Ravi Patel: Do you support BYOK (bring your own key) such that Redwood never sees the plaintext model keys?

[07:05] Jordan Lee: Yes, BYOK is supported. You can manage keys in your KMS/HSM and we can integrate the wrapped keys into the install manifest. Redwood does not retain unwrapped model keys in Private mode.
[07:30] Nia Brooks: What about offline dependency updates - e.g., CVE patches for the runtime libs? We have strict change windows and approval gates.

[07:45] Priya Raman: We handle runtime patching via signed patch sets. You can schedule patch windows; patches are applied in a staged manner with automatic rollback if health checks fail. We also provide a signed CVE summary per patch.
[08:10] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Is there a minimal hardware spec you recommend for our use case (high throughput, low latency for shorter contexts)?

[08:25] Priya Raman: For shorter contexts and high throughput, A100 80GB works well for mixed workloads; H100 gives better scaling for long contexts and NVLink is useful for model paralellism. We'll send a tailored spec but typical starter config is 4x A100s with 1 Gbps control network and isolated management plane.
[08:55] Evan Cole: We also need guidance on storage - do weights live on local NVMe, NFS, or object store? Our environment blocks outbound S3 calls.
[09:10] Jordan Lee: We support weights on local NVMe for performance. For model cataloging we provide an on-prem object store shim; everything can be contained locally. No external S3 required.
[09:35] Ravi Patel: Auditing: we need immutable audit logs for model invocations retained for 7 years per our policy. Can you support that retention?

[09:50] Priya Raman: Yes, logs can be exported to your archival storage - E.g., WORM-enabled object store. We include timestamped, signed audit records for each request. The storage retention is controlled by your infra.
[10:15] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Network isolation: do you require any egress at runtime for license checks, telemetry, etc?

[10:30] Jordan Lee: No runtime egress required. License checks can be performed via offline activation tokens you import during install. Telemetry is optional and off by default in Private installations.

[11:00] Evan Cole: Procurement note: our procurement team needs a clear breakdown of what is included in the Private deployment price - software license, support, optional on-site installation. Can you share that?

[11:15] Jordan Lee: Yes - we'll follow up with a price sheet for Private (license + annual support) and a separate line for professional services (on-site validation). Expect that in the package Jordan will send.
[11:40] Nia Brooks: Can we do an offline mock upgrade to validate the process? We want to run the install on a staging rack, validate tests, then do production cutover.

[11:55] Priya Raman: That's exactly the pattern we recommend. We'll provide a test harness and an upgrade manifest. In the mock run you validate checksums, signatures, and run your regression prompts.
[12:20] Ravi Patel: A small nit: how do you handle secrets for model decryption on disk? Are keys rotated automatically?

[12:35] Priya Raman: Key rotation is supported via your KMS. The flow is: model encrypted with data key, data key wrapped by your KMS key. Rotation is a KMS operation and doesn't require Redwood to handle unwrapped keys.
[12:55] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Any customers in highly regulated pharma doing a similar setup?

[13:10] Jordan Lee: Yes, a few clinical research orgs and biotechs have Private air-gapped deployments with similar constraints. We can share redacted case studies and architecture diagrams as part of the security pack.
[13:40] Evan Cole: For performance, do you provide profiling tools to see hot tokens and KV cache metrics?

[13:55] Priya Raman: We include an observability agent that runs locally and captures token-level latency, KV cache hit rate, and batching stats. In Private mode the agent stores data locally and you export samples during audit windows.
[14:25] Nia Brooks: Is there support for mixed mode - some workloads on Dedicated hosted and sensitive ones on Private?

[14:40] Jordan Lee: Yes - customers often use hybrid routing. We can route non-sensitive queries to Hosted/Dedicated and the sensitive workloads to Private. We also have fallback policies if Private capacity is constrained but for air-gapped you typically keep local capacity headroom.
[15:05] Ravi Patel: Regarding attestations, can we get a signed SBOM and provenance for runtime components?
[15:20] Priya Raman: We provide signed SBOMs for release bundles and commit hash provenance for binaries. That's included in the security package.
[15:45] Dr. Maria Sanchez: How long does an on-site validation typically take?
[16:00] Jordan Lee: Usually 1-2 days for install and smoke tests, and 3-5 days if you want a full regression suite run. We'll tailor based on your test depth.
[16:25] Evan Cole: Our timeline: procurement wants to approve vendor by end of March, with deployment Q2. Are you able to meet that cadence?
[16:40] Jordan Lee: Yes, that's feasible. We'll prioritize the security pack and an initial statement of work so procurement has what they need.
[17:00] Nia Brooks: One more question on model updates: can you provide delta patches instead of re-shipping entire model weights? Network bandwidth in our maintenance windows is limited.
[17:15] Priya Raman: We can do delta updates where applicable; depends on model format and quantization changes. We'll evaluate per release and recommend the best path.
[17:35] Ravi Patel: Can you list the exact logs and fields included in the audit record? We need to map to our SIEM.

[17:50] Jordan Lee: We'll include a sample audit schema in the security pack - request id, timestamp, model version, route, token counts, and a signed hash. We'll also include mapping guidance for common SIEMs.
[18:15] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Great. I think that's most of our high-level questions. Anything from Redwood on risk or known limitations?

[18:30] Priya Raman: The main limitations are around deterministic outputs if you use sampling; also delta updates can be trickier across quantization formats. For ultra-low latency under 5ms per token you need specific HW configs and tuning.
[18:55] Evan Cole: Ok let's recap next steps: security pack, hardware spec, schedule on-site validation, and procurement doc. Jordan?

[19:10] Jordan Lee: Yes - I'll send the SOC2/ISO pack, Priya will send hardware and upgrade manifest examples; we'll propose dates for the validation week (we suggested week of 2026-03-15). We'll also include pricing options for Private + PS.
[19:30] Dr. Maria Sanchez: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll aim to have the procurement decision by end of March.
[19:40] Jordan Lee: Thanks all - we'll follow up via email with links to the docs and next steps.
